minutes.headline: Zoning Board approved a special permit letting a Lemer Road garage be rebuilt two stories with a rear setback about 3 inches smaller.
minutes.summary: The board heard one hearing: Susan Carr's special permit for dimensional variation at 570 Lemer Road, to rebuild an attached garage with living space above. No one from the public spoke, and an abutter's letter of support was read. A motion to approve was made and seconded, and the chair read the standard conditions before adjournment.

public_comment.topic: Chair opened the hearing to the public; no one spoke in favor or against.

votes.motion: Approve the special permit for dimensional variation for the rear setback at 570 Lemer Road.

decisions.decision: After the vote on the rear-setback special permit, the chair proceeded to read the decision's conditions as for a granted permit; the vote tally itself was not captured.

The chair read that the special permit is granted, subject to compliance with applicable laws, periodic review, filing with the town clerk within 14 days, a 20-day appeal period, recording at the registry of deeds, and lapse within two years unless work begins.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals moved on a special permit for a garage rebuild at 570 Lemer Road, and the chair then read the decision as a granted permit; the vote count was not captured.
The chair read that the permit is granted, with conditions: a 14-day filing with the town clerk, a 20-day appeal period, recording at the registry of deeds, and lapse in two years unless work begins.
The applicant's representative presented a two-story rebuild of an attached garage with living space above, needing relief from the rear setback.
No one from the public spoke when the hearing was opened to comment; an abutter's letter of support was read earlier.

why_it_matters: This is a single-lot zoning decision: it touches the neighbours of 570 Lemer Road, who have a 20-day appeal window, and it does not touch any budget or tax bill.
Because the vote tally was not audible, the written decision filed with the town clerk is the record that shows the actual vote.
